name: Honeycake (Medovik)
steps: Mix honey, sugar and eggs over heat until smooth.
Stir in flour and knead dough.
Roll thin layers and bake.
Stack with cream filling.

name: Honey Teriyaki Salmon
steps: Mix soy sauce, honey, garlic, ginger and sesame oil.
Marinate salmon for 20 minutes.
Pan-fry or grill until cooked through.
Brush with extra marinade while cooking.

name: Honey Ginger Tofu
steps: Cube tofu and coat in cornflour.
Fry until crisp and set aside.
Mix soy sauce, honey, garlic and ginger.
Toss tofu in sauce and serve.

name: Hot and Sour Soup
steps: Heat stock, add mushrooms and tofu.
Add soy sauce, vinegar and chilli paste.
Thicken with cornflour paste.
Add spring onions before serving.

name: Houmous
steps: Blend chickpeas, tahini, garlic and lemon juice.
Add oil and blend until smooth.
Adjust salt and consistency.

name: Hungarian Goulash
steps: Sauté onions and garlic.
Add beef and brown well.
Stir in paprika and tomato paste.
Add vegetables and water.
Simmer until tender.

name: Hunter’s Chicken
steps: Season chicken and pan-fry lightly.
Wrap each piece in bacon.
Cover with barbecue sauce.
Top with cheddar and bake until cooked.

name: Hure
steps: Boil pork head meat with vegetables and spices.
Shred and pack into moulds.
Chill until set.

name: Hyderabadi Chicken Curry
steps: Fry onions until golden.
Add garlic and ginger paste.
Add chicken and cook until browned.
Add tomatoes, yogurt and spices.
Simmer until chicken is tender.

name: Hyderabadi Khatti Daal
steps: Boil dal with turmeric until soft.
Mash lightly and add tamarind.
Temper oil with garlic, cumin and curry leaves.
Pour tempering over dal.
Simmer briefly and serve.

name: Hyderabadi Mutton Biryani
steps: Marinate mutton with yogurt, spices and paste.
Fry onions until crisp.
Layer mutton, rice, herbs and fried onions.
Cook on low heat until rice and meat are tender.

name: Hyderabadi Mutton Dalcha
steps: Cook dal until soft.
Fry onions and paste, add mutton and spices.
Add tomatoes and cook thoroughly.
Combine dal and meat, simmer until tender.

name: Hyderabadi Tahari
steps: Fry onions and spices.
Add vegetables and cook.
Add rice and water.
Cover and cook until rice is done.

name: Gambas al ajillo
steps: Peel the prawns, leaving the tails intact, and, using a coc...ook the prawns in their shells. Season with a little sea salt.
Put the garlic, olive oil and chillies in a flameproof terr... as the oil and terracotta will remain hot for several minutes.

name: Garides Saganaki
steps: Place the prawns in a pot and add enough water to cover. Boil for 5 minutes. Drain, reserving the liquid, and set aside.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a saucepan. Add the onion; coo...onally, for about 30 minutes, or until the sauce is thickened.
While the sauce is simmering, the prawns should become cool...m, and then pull off the shells, leaving the head and tail on.
When the sauce has thickened, stir in the prawns. Bring to ...cheese starts to melt. Serve warm with slices of crusty bread.
Though completely untraditional, you can add a few tablespo... pasta sauce. Toss with pasta after adding the feta, and serve.

name: Garlicky prawns with sherry
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat ...turn pink. Add the sherry and bubble for 1 minute until syrupy.
Season to taste. Scatter with the parsley and serve with charred bread, if you like.

name: Ghormeh Sabzi
steps: Fry onions in oil until golden.
Add lamb and turmeric, cook until browned.
Add chopped herbs and fry until darkened.
Add beans, dried limes and water to cover.
Simmer until meat and beans are tender.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with rice.

name: Giouvetsi
steps: Heat oil in a pot and brown the beef.
Add onions and garlic and cook until softened.
Stir in tomato puree and tomatoes.
Add cinnamon, bay leaf and enough water to cover.
Simmer until beef is tender.
Add orzo and cook until tender, adding more water if needed.

name: Gyros
steps: Marinate pork in oil, herbs, spices, garlic and lemon juice.
Grill or roast until cooked and slightly charred.
Slice the meat thinly.
Serve in warm pita with tomato, onion and tzatziki.

name: Gözleme
steps: Mix flour, water and salt into a soft dough.
Rest the dough, then divide and roll into thin circles.
Fill with spinach and feta, fold and seal.
Cook on a lightly oiled griddle until golden on both sides.

name: Gazpacho
steps: Soak bread in water and squeeze out excess.
Blend all vegetables, bread, oil, vinegar and salt until smooth.
Chill well before serving.
Serve cold with chopped vegetables as garnish if desired.

name: Grilled Portuguese sardines
steps: Clean the sardines and pat dry.
Mix oil, crushed garlic and salt, and rub over sardines.
Grill on a barbecue or griddle until cooked through.
Serve with lemon wedges.

name: Grilled Portuguese sardines (marinated)
steps: Put all of the ingredients, except the sardines, into a bow...ardines and toss really well. Cover and chill for a few hours.
Heat a BBQ or griddle pan until hot. Cook the sardines for ...e with a little more paprika and squeeze over the lemon wedges.

name: Fainá
steps: Preheat your oven to 250°C (480°F) and place a baking pan (preferably cast iron or a pizza pan) inside to heat up.
In a large bowl, gradually whisk the water into the chickpe...il and 1 teaspoon of salt. Continue whisking until smooth.
Let the batter rest for at least 2 hours, or overnight in t...ensure the chickpea flour fully hydrates and the flavors meld.
For a crispy edge, preheat the baking pan with oil in the oven before adding the batter.

name: Falafel
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pan, then fry the onion and garl...Add the egg, then squish the mixture together with your hands.
Mould the mix into 6 balls, then flatten into patties. Heat...nd firm. Serve hot or cold with couscous, pitta bread or salad.

name: Falafel Pita Sandwich with Tahini Sauce
steps: Whisk together tahini, water, lemon juice, garlic, and salt until smooth.
Warm the pita breads and cut open to form pockets.
Stuff each pita with falafel, tomato, cucumber, and lettuce.
Drizzle with tahini sauce and serve.

name: Fettucine alfredo
steps: Cook the fettuccine in boiling salted water until al dente.
Melt butter in a pan, add cream and bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in grated parmesan until melted and smooth.
Toss the drained pasta with the sauce.
Season with salt and black pepper and serve immediately.

name: Filo Pastry
steps: Mix flour and salt in a bowl.
Add olive oil and vinegar, then gradually add water.
Knead into a soft, elastic dough.
Divide into balls, cover, and rest.
Roll each ball into a thin sheet for use.

name: Fish pie
steps: Boil potatoes until tender, then mash with milk and butter.
Poach fish in milk, then flake into a baking dish with prawns.
Make a white sauce with butter, flour and milk.
Pour sauce over fish, top with mashed potato and cheese.
Bake until golden and bubbling.

name: Fish Soup
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté onion, carrots and celery.
Add potatoes and fish, cover with water.
Simmer until vegetables and fish are cooked.
Season with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Serve hot.

name: Francesinha
steps: Grill the steak and sausages.
Layer bread with ham, steak, sausage and cheese to make sandwiches.
Cover sandwiches with more cheese.
Pour hot tomato-beer sauce over the sandwiches.
Grill until cheese is melted and serve hot.

name: French Onion Soup
steps: Cook onions slowly in butter and oil until caramelised.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add wine and stock, simmer for 30 minutes.
Top toasted baguette slices with gruyere.
Float the bread on the soup and grill until cheese melts.

name: Fried Anchovies
steps: Clean and rinse the anchovies.
Season flour with salt and coat anchovies.
Fry in hot oil until golden and crispy.
Drain on paper towel and serve hot.

name: Fried Rice
steps: Heat oil in a wok, add garlic and onion and fry until fragrant.
Add vegetables and stir-fry until tender.
Push vegetables to the side, scramble eggs in the same pan.
Add rice and soy sauce, mix everything together.
Stir-fry until heated through and serve.

name: Frozen Peanut Butter Pie
steps: Mix crushed cookies with melted butter and press into a pie dish.
Beat peanut butter, cream cheese and icing sugar until smooth.
Fold in whipped cream and spoon into crust.
Freeze until firm before serving.

name: Fyrstekake (Norwegian Almond Cake)
steps: Crust
Stir together flour, sugar, and baking powder in a mixing bowl.
Cut the butter into the flour mixture in a food processor o...the butter is fully incorporated and the mixture clumps up.
Press the dough into a ball. If it feels too dry, you can a...urning the dough out onto a very lightly floured countertop
Pack the dough in plastic wrap and chill in refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
Almond filling
Run the almonds and sugar together in a food processor unti...you can decide for yourself how coarse or fine you want them).
Stir in the butter, egg, cognac and/or almond extract (if using).
Assembly
Line the bottom of your cake form with baking paper and grease the sides of the form.
Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Cut 2/3 of the crust dough into slices and press down into ...2-3 cm (1 inch) up the sides of the form, pressing until even.
Scoop the almond filling on top of the crust, spreading it evenly across the cake form.
Roll out of the rest of the dough and slice into long strip...he strips break - simply press them back together on the cake.
Gently brush the dough with egg wash.
Bake for about 45 minutes. The top of the cake should be golden brown while the almond filling will remain soft.

name: Easy Spanish chicken
steps: Heat oil in a large frying pan and fry the onion until softened.
Add chorizo and cook until it releases its oils.
Add red pepper and garlic and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add chicken thighs and brown on all sides.
Stir in paprika, passata, and chicken stock.
Season with salt and pepper.
Simmer for 30-40 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Serve hot with rice or crusty bread.

name: Egg Curry
steps: Heat oil in a pan and sauté onions until golden brown.
Add ginger garlic paste and sauté for a minute.
Add tomato puree and cook until oil separates.
Add spices and cook for 2 minutes.
Add water and bring to a boil.
Add boiled eggs and simmer for 5-10 minutes.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve.

name: Eggs benedict
steps: Toast the English muffins and spread with butter.
Top each muffin half with a slice of ham.
Poach the eggs in simmering water with vinegar.
Place a poached egg on each muffin half.
To make hollandaise, whisk egg yolks and lemon juice over a bain-marie.
Gradually add melted butter while whisking until thickened.
Season with salt and pepper and spoon over the eggs.
Serve immediately.

name: English Breakfast
steps: Grill sausages and bacon until cooked and browned.
Fry mushrooms and tomatoes in a pan with a little oil.
Heat baked beans in a small saucepan.
Fry or poach the eggs as desired.
Toast the bread and spread with butter.
Serve everything together on a large plate.

name: Eton Mess
steps: Hull and slice the strawberries.
Sprinkle with caster sugar and leave to macerate.
Whip the cream until soft peaks form.
Fold in the crushed meringue and most of the strawberries.
Spoon into serving glasses and top with remaining strawberries.
Serve immediately.

name: Eccles Cakes
steps: Make a pastry dough with butter, flour, and lemon juice.
Chill the dough in the fridge.
Mix currants, mixed peel, sugar, and spices for the filling.
Roll out the pastry and cut into circles.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle.
Fold and seal, then bake until golden brown.
Serve warm or cold.

name: Dal fry
steps: Rinse the lentils in cold water. Add dal and water in a pot.
Add salt and turmeric. Bring to a boil and simmer until soft.
In a pan, heat ghee and add cumin and mustard seeds.
Add bay leaves, green chilies, and curry leaves.
Add onion and cook until golden brown.
Add chili powder, coriander powder, and tomatoes. Cook until tomatoes soften.
Add cooked dal and garam masala. Simmer for 5-10 minutes.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot.

name: Dal makhani
steps: Soak lentils and kidney beans overnight.
Cook them in a pressure cooker with water and salt until soft.
In a pan, heat butter and oil.
Add ginger, garlic, and green chilies. Sauté for a minute.
Add onion and cook until golden brown.
Add tomato puree and cook until oil separates.
Add chili powder, garam masala, and cooked lentils.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes.
Stir in cream and cook for another 5 minutes.
Serve hot with naan or rice.

name: Dumpling stuffed with meat
steps: Make a dough with flour, water, egg, and salt.
Let the dough rest and roll it out thinly.
Cut circles and add a spoon of meat mixture in each.
Seal the dumplings and boil in salted water until cooked.
Serve hot with sour cream or butter.

name: Duck Confit
steps: Rub duck legs with salt, thyme, and garlic.
Marinate for at least 24 hours in the fridge.
Rinse off the salt and pat dry.
Submerge duck legs in melted duck fat in an ovenproof dish.
Cook at low temperature until very tender.
Store in fat or grill before serving.

name: Drunken noodles (pad kee mao)
steps: Cook rice noodles according to packet instructions and set aside.
Heat oil in a wok and fry garlic and chili until fragrant.
Add chicken and stir-fry until cooked.
Add vegetables and cook until tender-crisp.
Add fish sauce, oyster sauce, and soy sauce.
Add noodles and basil leaves, tossing everything together.
Serve hot.

name: Dhakani kheema
steps: Heat oil in a pan and sauté onions until golden brown.
Add garlic and ginger and sauté for a minute.
Add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add spices and cook until fragrant.
Add minced beef and cook until browned.
Add water and simmer until cooked through.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve.

name: Cabbage Soup (Shchi)
steps: Add the butter to a large Dutch oven or other heavy-duty pot over medium heat. When the butter has melted, add the onion and sauté until translucent.
Add the cabbage, carrot, and celery. Sauté until the vegetables begin to soften, stirring frequently, about 3 minutes.
Add the bay leaf and vegetable stock and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, until the vegetables are crisp-tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the potatoes and bring it back to a boil over high heat. Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, until the potatoes are tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the tomatoes (or undrained canned tomatoes) and bring the soup back to a boil over high heat. Reduce the heat to low and simmer, uncovered, for 5 minutes. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Remove and discard the bay leaf from the pot.
Serve topped with fresh sour cream and fresh dill.

name: Cacik
steps: Put a sieve over a large bowl, line it with a thick sheet of non-dyed kitchen paper or a clean muslin cloth, and spoon in the yogurt. Cover with another sheet of kitchen paper and leave to strain in the fridge for a minimum of 12 hrs.

Add the lemon juice, most of the olive oil and the dried mint to a bowl and stir well for the dried mint to soften and soak up the juices. Mix in the strained yogurt, then pour away the strained yogurt liquid and leave that bowl to one side.

Halve the cucumber(s) lengthways and remove the seeds by running a teaspoon from the top to the bottom of the flesh, halve the cucumbers widthways to make them shorter and easier to handle, then coarsely grate each one into the bowl the yogurt was straining over. Using clean hands (or a clean muslin cloth), squeeze as much of the liquid out of the cucumber as possible.
Add the strained, grated cucumber, garlic and ¾ tsp flaky salt to the rest of the ingredients and mix well. Garnish with a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil and a sprinkling of dried mint.

name: Cajun spiced fish tacos
steps: Cooking in a cajun spice and cayenne pepper marinade makes this fish super succulent and flavoursome. Top with a zesty dressing and serve in a tortilla for a quick, fuss-free main that's delightfully summery.
On a large plate, mix the cajun spice and cayenne pepper with a little seasoning and use to coat the fish all over.

Heat a little oil in a frying pan, add in the fish and cook over a medium heat until golden. Reduce the heat and continue frying until the fish is cooked through, about 10 minutes. Cook in batches if you don’t have enough room in the pan.
Meanwhile, prepare the dressing by combining all the ingredients with a little seasoning.

Soften the tortillas by heating in the microwave for 5-10 seconds. Pile high with the avocado, lettuce and spring onion, add a spoonful of salsa, top with large flakes of fish and drizzle over the dressing.

name: Callaloo Jamaican Style
steps: Cut leaves and soft stems from the kale branches, them soak in a bowl of cold water for about 5-10 minutes or until finish with prep.
Proceed to slicing the onions, mincing the garlic and dicing the tomatoes. Set aside
Remove kale from water cut in chunks.
Place bacon on saucepan and cook until crispy. Then add onions, garlic, thyme, stir for about a minute or more
Add tomatoes; scotch bonnet pepper, smoked paprika. Sauté for about 2-3 more minutes.
Finally add vegetable, salt, mix well, and steamed for about 6-8 minutes or until leaves are tender. Add a tiny bit of water as needed. Adjust seasonings and turn off the heat.

Using a sharp knife cut both ends off the plantain. This will make it easy to grab the skin of the plantains. Slit a shallow line down the long seam of the plantain; peel only as deep as the peel. Remove plantain peel by pulling it back.
Slice the plantain into medium size lengthwise slices and set aside.
Coat a large frying pan with cooking oil spray. Spray the tops of the plantains with a generous layer of oil spray and sprinkle with salt, freshly ground pepper.
Let the plantains "fry" on medium heat, shaking the frying pan to redistribute them every few minutes.
As the plantains brown, continue to add more cooking oil spray, salt and pepper (if needed) until they have reached the desired color and texture.
Remove and serve with kale

name: Canadian Butter Tarts
steps: Preheat the oven to fan 170C/ conventional 190C/gas 5. Roll out the pastry on a lightly floured surface so it’s slightly thinner than straight from the pack. Then cut out 18-20 rounds with a 7.5cm fluted cutter, re-rolling the trimmings. Use the rounds to line two deep 12-hole tart tins (not muffin tins). If you only have a regular-sized, 12-hole tart tin you will be able to make a few more slightly shallower tarts.

Beat the eggs in a large bowl and combine with the rest of the ingredients except the walnuts. Tip this mixture into a pan and stir continuously for 3-4 minutes until the butter melts, and the mixture bubbles and starts to thicken. It should be thick enough to coat the back of a wooden spoon. Don’t overcook, and be sure to stir all the time as the mixture can easily burn. Remove from the heat and stir in the nuts.

Spoon the filling into the unbaked tart shells so it’s level with the pastry. Bake for 15-18 minutes until set and pale golden. Leave in the tin to cool for a few minutes before lifting out on to a wire rack. Serve warm or cold.

name: Carbonada Criolla
steps: Brown the "Beef": In a large pot, brown the beef cubes. Remove and set aside.
Sauté "Vegetables": In the same pot, cook the onion until translucent. Add carrots, potatoes, and pumpkin, cooking for a few minutes.
Simmer: Return the beef to the pot. Add broth and dried apricots. Season with salt and pepper. Simmer for 1-2 hours, until the beef is tender.
Serve: Enjoy hot, with a crusty piece of bread.
Pro "Tips":
Brown the beef in batches to ensure it gets a good sear, which adds depth to the stew's flavor.
Adding the fruits towards the end of cooking preserves their texture and adds a subtle sweetness to the dish.

name: Carrot Cake
steps: For the carrot cake, preheat the oven to 160C/325F/Gas 3. Grease and line a 26cm/10in springform cake tin.
Mix all of the ingredients for the carrot cake, except the carrots and walnuts, together in a bowl until well combined. Stir in the carrots and walnuts.

Spoon the mixture into the cake tin and bake for 1 hour 15 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the middle comes out clean. Remove the cake from the oven and set aside to cool for 10 minutes, then carefully remove the cake from the tin and set aside to cool completely on a cooling rack.
Meanwhile, for the icing, beat the cream cheese, caster sugar and butter together in a bowl until fluffy. Spread the icing over the top of the cake with a palette knife.

name: Cashew Ghoriba Biscuits
steps: Preheat the oven at 180 C / Gas 4. Line a baking tray with greaseproof paper.
In a bowl, mix the cashews and icing sugar. Add the egg yolks and orange blossom water and mix to a smooth homogeneous paste.
Take lumps of the cashew paste and shape into small balls. Roll the balls in icing sugar and transfer to the baking tray. Push an almond in the centre of each ghribia.
Bake until the biscuits are lightly golden, about 20 minutes. Keep an eye on them, they burn quickly.

name: Cevapi Sausages
steps: Place the ground meat in a bowl. Chop the onion very finely and grate the garlic cloves. Add to the bowl. Add the chopped parsley, all sorts of paprika, baking soda, dried breadcrumbs, water, Vegeta, salt, and pepper.
Mix well with the hand mixer fitted with the dough hooks. Cover the bowl with cling film/ plastic foil and leave to rest for 1 or 2 hours in the refrigerator.

Take portions of the meat mixture, about 50-55 g/ 1.7-1.9 oz/ ¼ cup portions, and form the cevapi. The rolls should be about as thick as your thumb and about 7-10 cm/ 3-4 inches long. I had 18 sausages. The recipe can be easily doubled.

Grill the cevapcici on the hot grill pan or on the barbecue for about 12-14 minutes, turning them several times in between, or until brown and cooked through. I checked by cutting one in the middle and then grilling the following batches for the same period of time.

Serve hot as suggested above. The cevapcici can be reheated in the oven at 180 degrees Celsius/ 350 degrees Fahrenheit for about 10 minutes or until heated through. Check one, if it is not hot enough, give the sausages a few more minutes.

name: Chakchouka
steps: In a large cast iron skillet or sauté pan with a lid, heat oil over medium high heat. Add the onion and sauté for 2-3 minutes, until softened. Add the peppers and garlic, and sauté for an additional 3-5 minutes. Add the tomatoes, cumin, paprika, salt, and chili powder. Mix well and bring the mixture to a simmer. Reduce the heat to medium low and continue to simmer, uncovered, 10-15 minutes until the mixture has thickened to your desired consistency. (Taste the sauce at this point and adjust for salt and spice, as desired.) Using the back of a spoon, make four craters in the mixture, large enough to hold an egg. Crack one egg into each of the craters. Cover the skillet and simmer for 5-7 minutes, until the eggs have set. Serve immediately with crusty bread or pita.

name: Cheese Borek
steps: In a medium bowl, whisk together egg, parsley, garlic and crushed red pepper. Mix in Gouda and Emmentaler.

One sheet at a time, place phyllo dough on a flat surface and brush with about 1 tablespoon butter. Cut lengthwise into 4 strips. Place a rounded teaspoon of the egg mixture at one end of each strip. Fold corner of strip over the filling, forming a triangular fold. Continue folding the length of the strip in triangular folds to form a small stuffed triangle. Repeat with remaining phyllo dough.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly butter a large baking sheet.
Arrange stuffed phyllo triangles in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Bake in the preheated oven 30 minutes, or until lightly browned. Serve warm

name: Chelsea Buns
steps: Sift the flour and salt into a large bowl. Make a well in the middle and add the yeast.
Meanwhile, warm the milk and butter in a saucepan until the butter melts and the mixture is lukewarm.
Add the milk mixture and egg to the flour mixture and stir until the contents of the bowl come together as a soft dough. (You may need to add a little extra flour.)
Tip the dough onto a generously floured work surface. Knead for five minutes, adding more flour if necessary, until the dough is smooth and elastic and no longer feels sticky.

Lightly oil a bowl with a little of the vegetable oil. Place the dough into the bowl and turn until it is covered in the oil. Cover the bowl with cling film and set aside in a warm place for one hour, or until the dough has doubled in size.
Lightly grease a baking tray.

For the filling, knock the dough back to its original size and turn out onto a lightly floured work surface. Roll the dough out into a rectangle 0.5cm/¼in thick. Brush all over with the melted butter, then sprinkle over the brown sugar, cinnamon and dried fruit.

Roll the dough up into a tight cylinder , cut ten 4cm/1½in slice and place them onto a lightly greased baking sheet, leaving a little space between each slice. Cover with a tea towel and set aside to rise for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 190C/375F/Gas 5.
Bake the buns in the oven for 20-25 minutes, or until risen and golden-brown.
Meanwhile, for the glaze, heat the milk and sugar in a saucepan until boiling. Reduce the heat and simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Remove the buns from the oven and brush with the glaze, then set aside to cool on a wire rack.

name: Baba Ghanoush
steps: Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate. Pierce the skin of eggplants several times with the tip of a knife.

Place eggplants directly on grill. Turn frequently with tongs and cook until completely blackened and soft, 25 to 30 minutes. Transfer to a bowl and cover tightly with aluminum foil and allow to cool, about 15 minutes.
When eggplants are cool enough to handle, split them in half and scoop out the flesh into a colander placed over a bowl. Drain 5 or 10 minutes.

Transfer eggplant to mixing bowl. Add crushed garlic and salt; mix vigorously with a fork until eggplant breaks down into a paste. Mix in lemon juice, tahini, olive oil, and cayenne pepper. Stir in yogurt.
Cover bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate until completely chilled. Stir in mint and parsley before serving.

name: Baked egg with tomato and chorizo hash
steps: Heat the oil in a medium-sized frying pan. Throw in the onion and fry over a medium heat until softened and lightly coloured.
Add the chorizo and fry until it starts to release its oils, then add the garlic and red pepper and continue to fry.
Add the tomatoes and paprika, season and simmer until the tomatoes reduce down to a thick sauce.
Make 4 wells in the mixture with the back of a large spoon and crack the eggs into them.

Cover the pan with a lid or large baking sheet if you don’t have one, and cook until the whites have just set and the yolks are still a little runny. Scatter over the parsley and serve with chunks of crusty bread.

name: Baked mango cheesecake
steps: Heat oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Butter and line the base of a deep 20cm springform tin.
Crush the biscuits to crumbs, then mix in the butter. Press into the base of the tin and bake for 10 mins. Allow to cool slightly.
In a food processor, whizz the mango flesh to a pulp. In a large bowl, whisk the lime zest and juice, sugar and cornflour until smooth.
Whisk in the soft cheese, then the eggs, one at a time. Fold through half the mango pulp.
Pour the filling onto the cooled biscuit base, then drizzle over the remaining mango. Use a skewer to create a swirled effect.
Bake for 45 mins until set, then turn off the oven, prop the door ajar and leave the cheesecake to cool completely.
Chill for at least 3 hrs or overnight. Serve topped with the sliced mango.

name: Baked pork chops
steps: Preheat oven to 190 degrees C.
Place pork chops in a baking pan. Spread 1 teaspoon of butter over each chop, then spread 1 teaspoon of mayonnaise over butter.
Top with garlic, seasoning salt and pepper. Sprinkle 1 teaspoon of paprika onto each chop.
Bake 35 minutes in preheated oven, or until the internal temperature of the chops has reached 63 degrees C.

name: Baked salmon with fennel & tomatoes
steps: Heat oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Chop the fennel into wedges and thinly slice the onion.
Toss the fennel and onion together with 2 tbsp olive oil in a roasting tin. Season and roast for 20 mins.
Zest the lemon and cut into wedges. Toss the fennel and onion with the lemon zest and cherry tomatoes. Dot over the butter.
Place the salmon on top of the vegetables, season, then drizzle with 1 tbsp olive oil.
Return to the oven for 12-15 mins until the salmon is just cooked. Scatter over the olives and basil, then serve with lemon wedges.

name: Baked stuffed peppers
steps: Heat oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6.
Halve the peppers from top to bottom and remove the seeds. Put in a roasting tin, cut-side up, drizzle with 2 tbsp of the oil and season. Roast for 20 mins.
Meanwhile, heat remaining oil in a frying pan, add onion and fry for 5 mins.
Add garlic and courgettes, then fry for 5 mins more. Stir in halved tomatoes and cook for another 3 mins.
Remove from the heat, stir in basil, breadcrumbs and half the Parmesan, then season.
Fill the pepper halves with the mixture, sprinkle over remaining Parmesan and return to the oven for 20 mins.

name: BBQ Beef Brisket
steps: Mix the sugar and spices together, then rub all over the beef brisket.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hrs or overnight.
Heat oven to 140C/120C fan/gas 1. Put the beef in a roasting tin and cover with foil.
Cook for 5 hrs until the meat is very tender. Slice and serve with BBQ sauce.

name: BBQ Chicken
steps: Mix the BBQ sauce, oil and spices in a bowl.
Slash the chicken legs a few times, then toss in the marinade. Leave for 1 hr or overnight.
Heat a barbecue or grill.
Cook the chicken for 20-25 mins, turning occasionally, until cooked through and charred.

name: BBQ Pork Sloppy Joes
steps: Heat a frying pan and cook the pork mince until browned.
Add the chopped onion and garlic and cook until softened.
Stir in the BBQ sauce, ketchup and mustard and simmer for 10 mins.
Serve in toasted burger buns.

name: Beef and Mustard Pie
steps: Brown the beef in a large pan.
Add the onion and carrots and cook for a few mins.
Pour in the stock and simmer until the beef is tender.
Stir in the mustard and cool the mixture.
Heat oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Fill a pie dish with the beef mixture and cover with pastry.
Bake for 30-35 mins until golden.

name: Beef and Ox Cheek Pudding
steps: Brown the beef and ox cheek in a pan.
Add the onion and carrots and cook briefly.
Add the stock and simmer until the meat is tender.
Line a pudding basin with suet pastry, fill with the meat mixture and cover with more pastry.
Steam for 3-4 hrs until cooked through.

name: Beef Asado
steps: Marinate the beef in soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, bay leaves and pepper for at least 1 hr.
Brown the beef in a pan, then pour in the marinade.
Simmer until the beef is tender.

name: Beef Banh Mi Bowls with Sriracha Mayo
steps: Cook the rice according to pack instructions.
Pickle the carrots and cucumber in rice vinegar.
Fry the beef mince and season with soy sauce.
Mix the sriracha and mayonnaise.
Serve the beef over rice with the pickled vegetables and sriracha mayo.

name: Beef Bourguignon
steps: Marinate the beef in red wine overnight.
Brown the beef and bacon in a pan.
Add the onion, carrots and mushrooms and cook briefly.
Pour in the marinade and simmer until the beef is tender.

name: Beef Brisket Pot Roast
steps: Brown the brisket in a large pan.
Add the vegetables and cook briefly.
Pour in the stock and simmer until the beef is tender.

name: Beef Bulgogi
steps: Marinate the beef in soy sauce, sugar, garlic, sesame oil and spring onions.
Stir-fry in a hot pan until cooked through.

name: Beef Caldereta
steps: Brown the beef in a pan.
Add the potatoes and carrots and cook briefly.
Stir in the tomato sauce and liver spread and simmer until the beef is tender.

name: Beef Coconut Curry
steps: Fry the onion and pepper in a pan.
Add the curry paste and cook briefly.
Add the beef and brown.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer until the beef is tender.

name: Beef Dumpling Stew
steps: Brown the beef in a pan.
Add the vegetables and stock and simmer until the beef is tender.
Add the dumplings and cook until they are done.

name: Beef Lo Mein
steps: Cook the noodles according to pack instructions.
Stir-fry the beef and vegetables in a hot pan.
Add the sauces and noodles and toss together.

name: Beef Roast
steps: Preheat oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6.
Rub the beef with garlic, rosemary and olive oil.
Roast for 1-1.5 hrs depending on size and desired doneness.

name: Beef Salad
steps: Grill or fry the beef to your liking and slice.
Toss the salad ingredients together and top with the beef.
Dress with olive oil and lemon juice.

name: Beef Stew and Dumplings
steps: Brown the beef in a pan.
Add the vegetables and stock and simmer until the beef is tender.
Add the dumplings and cook until done.

name: Beef Tartare
steps: Finely chop the beef fillet.
Mix with the capers, gherkins, onion and parsley.
Serve topped with egg yolks.

name: Beef Wellington
steps: Brown the beef fillet in a pan.
Chop and fry the mushrooms until dry.
Wrap the beef in parma ham and mushrooms, then in puff pastry.
Brush with egg and bake at 200C/180C fan/gas 6 for 35-40 mins.

name: Beef Wet Burrito
steps: Cook the beef mince and season as desired.
Fill tortillas with beef, beans and some cheese.
Roll up and place in a baking dish.
Pour over salsa and top with remaining cheese.
Bake until hot and bubbling.

name: Beef Wontons
steps: Mix the beef mince with soy sauce, garlic and ginger.
Place small spoonfuls in wonton wrappers and seal.
Boil or steam until cooked through.

name: Beer Braised Brisket
steps: Brown the brisket in a pan.
Add the onion and garlic and cook briefly.
Pour in the beer and simmer until the beef is tender.

name: Beer Can Chicken
steps: Rub the chicken with spice rub.
Open the beer can and place it inside the chicken cavity.
Stand the chicken upright on a barbecue and cook until done.

name: Beetroot and Goats Cheese Salad
steps: Slice the beetroot and goats cheese.
Arrange on a bed of lettuce with walnuts.
Dress with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.

name: Banana Bread
steps: Heat oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4.
Mash the bananas and mix with melted butter, sugar and egg.
Fold in the flour and pour into a loaf tin.
Bake for 40-45 mins.

name: BBQ Spareribs
steps: Preheat oven to 160C/140C fan/gas 3.
Brush the ribs with BBQ sauce and wrap in foil.
Bake for 2-3 hrs until tender.

name: Burek
steps: Fry the finely chopped onions and minced meat in oil. Add the salt and pepper.
Layer the filo pastry with the meat mixture and roll.
Bake at 200ºC/392ºF for half an hour and cut in quarters and serve.

name: Adana kebab
steps: step 1

Finely chop the peppers in a food processor, then tip them in a sieve and press into the sieve so that the peppers release all of their juices. Tip into a bowl along with the mince, red pepper paste, pul biber, 1½ tsp flaky sea salt, and 2 tbsp of the oil. Mix together, kneading well for at least 2-3 mins. If you need to, wet your hands with cold water to prevent the mixture from sticking. The mixture should be sticky when ready. Cover and chill for at least 2 hrs, or up to 12 hrs.
step 2

When ready to cook, heat the grill to high or an oven to 220C/200C fan/gas 6. Divide the mixture into 12 equal portions, around 85g each. If you’d like to skewer them, divide into 8 equal portions and roll into balls. Using wet hands, thread the balls onto the end of the skewers, massaging the mixture down the skewers in between the palms of your hands, until evenly distributed. Ensure that the mixture is fully wrapped tightly around the skewers without any exposed metal. Alternatively, lay them on a large baking tray lined with parchment paper if cooking in the oven, or foil if cooking under the grill. Shape into 20cm-long köfte. Wet your fingers with a little cold water and make indents all along the köfte for the traditional shape.
step 3

Gently brush each köfte with the remaining 1 tbsp oil and cook under the grill, on the top shelf for 10-12 mins, turning regularly, or cook in the oven for 16-18 mins, until crispy on the outside and juicy in the middle

name: Air fryer patatas bravas
steps: step 1

Soak the potatoes in just-boiled water for 30 mins, then drain and leave to air-dry for 5 mins. Heat the air fryer to 200C. Tip the potatoes into a bowl and drizzle over 1 tbsp of the oil and add 1/2 tsp each of salt and freshly ground black pepper. Mix to coat the potatoes all over, then tip into the air fryer basket and cook for 20-30 mins until crisp and golden.
step 2

Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a small pan over a medium-low heat and fry the onion for 8-10 mins until softened but not golden. Stir in the garlic and cook for a minute before adding the paprika and cooking for 30 seconds more. Stir in the tomato purée, cook for 1 min, then tip in the chopped tomatoes. Cook for 5-10 mins over a medium heat until thickened slightly.
step 3
Once the potatoes are cooked, tip out onto a platter and pour over the tomato sauce. Sprinkle with the basil leaves, then serve.

name: Ajo blanco
steps: step 1
Tip the bread into a bowl and pour over 350ml water. Leave to soak for 10 mins.
step 2
Blend the ingredients together with 350ml water and 1 tsp salt.
step 3
Let the soup cool in the fridge for 1 hr or so, then serve with a drizzle of oil and some black pepper.

name: Alfajores
steps: Make the "Dough": Cream butter and sugar. Add egg yolks and lemon zest. Gradually mix in flour and cornstarch to form a dough. Chill for 1 hour.
Bake the "Cookies": Roll out the dough, cut into circles, and bake at 180°C (350°F) for 12-15 minutes. Let cool.
Assemble: Spread dulce de leche on one cookie, then sandwich with another. Roll the edges in coconut flakes.
Pro "Tips":
Chill the dough before rolling it out to make it easier to handle and to prevent the cookies from spreading too much while baking.
Dip the alfajores in melted chocolate and let them set on a wire rack for an extra decadent treat.

name: Algerian Bouzgene Berber Bread with Roasted Pepper Sauce
steps: Preheat your oven's broiler. Place red bell peppers and tomatoes on a baking sheet, and roast under the broiler for about 8 minutes, turning occasionally. This should blacken the skin and help it peel off more easily. Cool, then scrape the skins off of the tomatoes and peppers, and place them in a large bowl. Remove cores and seeds from the bell peppers.

Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the jalapenos and garlic, and cook until tender, stirring frequently. Remove from heat, and transfer the garlic and jalapeno to the bowl with the tomatoes and red peppers. Using two sharp steak knives (one in each hand), cut up the tomatoes and peppers to a coarse and soupy consistency. Stir, and set sauce aside.

Place the semolina in a large bowl, and stir in salt and 4 tablespoons of olive oil. Gradually add water while mixing and squeezing with your hand until the dough holds together without being sticky or dry, and molds easily with the hand. Divide into 6 pieces and form into balls.

For each round, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large heavy skillet over medium heat. Roll out dough one round at a time, to no thicker than 1/4 inch. Fry in the hot skillet until dark brown spots appear on the surface, and they are crispy. Remove from the skillet, and wrap in a clean towel while preparing the remaining flat breads.
To eat the bread and sauce, break off pieces of the bread, and scoop them into the sauce. It will slide off, but just keep reaching in!

name: Algerian Carrots
steps: Place a steamer insert into a saucepan, and fill with 1 1/2 cups of water, or just below the bottom of the steamer. Cover, and bring the water to a boil over high heat. Add the sliced carrots, reduce the heat to medium, and cover the pan again. Steam until tender but not mushy, 4 to 6 minutes depending on the thickness of the slices. Reserve 1/2 cup of the cooking liquid.

Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Reduce the heat to low and stir in the salt, pepper, cinnamon, cumin, garlic, and thyme. Cook the spices and garlic, stirring frequently, until fragrant, about 10 minutes. Add the 1/2 cup reserved cooking liquid and the bay leaf, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in the carrots, tossing well to coat with the spice mixture, and cook until heated through, about 2 to 3 minutes. Sprinkle with lemon juice and remove the bay leaf before serving.

name: Algerian Flafla (Bell Pepper Salad)
steps: Preheat an oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). Place the whole peppers on aluminum foil. Bake until the skin is spotted black and the peppers are soft, 30 to 45 minutes, turning the peppers once if necessary.
Remove peppers from the oven and set aside to cool for 10 minutes. Peel off the skin and remove the stem and seeds. Chop the roasted peppers into half-inch pieces.

Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Stir in the onion and cook, stirring frequently, until the onion has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic, salt, and pepper; stir in the chopped peppers and tomato. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the tomato is soft and the mixture is well incorporated, about 5 minutes.

name: Algerian Kefta (Meatballs)
steps: Combine ground beef with 1/2 of the minced garlic and 1 tablespoon chopped onion in a large bowl. Mix with your hands until fully incorporated. Shape meat mixture into 1 1/2-inch oblong patties; you should have 12 to 14 meatballs.

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown patties in batches in the hot skillet until crispy on both sides and no longer pink in the center, about 10 minutes. Set meatballs aside in a rimmed serving dish.

Reduce heat to medium and stir remaining chopped onion into drippings in the skillet. Season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring constantly, until onion has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in remaining garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Stir in Roma tomatoes, dried parsley, and ras el hanout. Pour in water. Cook until tomatoes are soft, about 5 minutes.
Pour tomato sauce over meatballs to serve.

name: Anzac biscuits
steps: step 1

Heat oven to 180C/fan 160C/gas 4. Put the oats, coconut, flour and sugar in a bowl. Melt the butter in a small pan and stir in the golden syrup. Add the bicarbonate of soda to 2 tbsp boiling water, then stir into the golden syrup and butter mixture.
step 2
Make a well in the middle of the dry ingredients and pour in the butter and golden syrup mixture. Stir gently to incorporate the dry ingredients.
step 3
Put dessertspoonfuls of the mixture on to buttered baking sheets, about 2.5cm/1in apart to allow room for spreading. Bake in batches for 8-10 mins until golden. Transfer to a wire rack to cool.

name: Apam balik
steps: Mix milk, oil and egg together. Sift flour, baking powder and salt into the mixture. Stir well until all ingredients are combined evenly.
Spread some batter onto the pan. Spread a thin layer of batter to the side of the pan. Cover the pan for 30-60 seconds until small air bubbles appear.
Add butter, cream corn, crushed peanuts and sugar onto the pancake. Fold the pancake into half once the bottom surface is browned.
Cut into wedges and best eaten when it is warm.

name: Apple & Blackberry Crumble
steps: Heat oven to 190C/170C fan/gas 5. Tip the flour and sugar into a large bowl. Add the butter, then rub into the flour using your fingertips to make a light breadcrumb texture. Do not overwork it or the crumble will become heavy. Sprinkle the mixture evenly over a baking sheet and bake for 15 mins or until lightly coloured.

Meanwhile, for the compote, peel, core and cut the apples into 2cm dice. Put the butter and sugar in a medium saucepan and melt together over a medium heat. Cook for 3 mins until the mixture turns to a light caramel. Stir in the apples and cook for 3 mins. Add the blackberries and cinnamon, and cook for 3 mins more. Cover, remove from the heat, then leave for 2-3 mins to continue cooking in the warmth of the pan.
To serve, spoon the warm fruit into an ovenproof gratin dish, top with the crumble mix, then reheat in the oven for 5-10 mins. Serve with vanilla ice cream.

name: Apple Frangipan Tart
steps: Preheat the oven to 200C/180C Fan/Gas 6.

Put the biscuits in a large re-sealable freezer bag and bash with a rolling pin into fine crumbs. Melt the butter in a small pan, then add the biscuit crumbs and stir until coated with butter. Tip into the tart tin and, using the back of a spoon, press over the base and sides of the tin to give an even layer. Chill in the fridge while you make the filling.

Cream together the butter and sugar until light and fluffy. You can do this in a food processor if you have one. Process for 2-3 minutes. Mix in the eggs, then add the ground almonds and almond extract and blend until well combined.

Peel the apples, and cut thin slices of apple. Do this at the last minute to prevent the apple going brown. Arrange the slices over the biscuit base. Spread the frangipane filling evenly on top. Level the surface and sprinkle with the flaked almonds.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until golden-brown and set.
Remove from the oven and leave to cool for 15 minutes. Remove the sides of the tin. An easy way to do this is to stand the tin on a can of beans and push down gently on the edges of the tin.
Transfer the tart, with the tin base attached, to a serving plate. Serve warm with cream, crème fraiche or ice cream.

name: Apricot & Turkish delight mess
steps: step 1

Place the mascarpone, yogurt, sugar and orange flower water into a large bowl and whisk until thickened. Fold the remaining ingredients through, then divide the mix between 2 dessert glasses or bowls and decorate with extra mint, if you like.

name: Arroz al horno (baked rice)
steps: step 1

Heat oven to 200C/180C/gas 6. Heat half the oil in a deep frying or sauté pan (or shallow casserole dish) measuring around 30cm in diameter. Over a high heat, colour the pork belly slices on each side in several batches, then transfer to a bowl. Add the remaining oil to the pan and lower the heat to medium, then add the black pudding and bacon and fry all over for several mins. Remove with a slotted spoon. Fry the onion and peppers for around 10 mins until soft and pale gold, then add the tomato and cook until soft. Add the garlic, smoked paprika and chilli flakes and cook for another 2 mins, then put the pork, black pudding and bacon back in the pan. Add the beans, stock and whichever herb you're using, and bring everything to the boil.
step 2

Sprinkle the rice around the pork belly, pushing it underneath the stock. Let the stock come to the boil again, season well, then transfer to the oven (leave it uncovered). Cook for 20 mins without stirring, then check to see how the rice is doing. The rice should be tender and the stock absorbed. If it’s not ready, put back in the oven for another 5 mins, then check again. Taste for seasoning.
step 3
Squeeze lemon juice over the top and drizzle over some extra virgin olive oil just before serving, if you like.

name: Arroz con gambas y calamar
steps: step 1

Peel and devein most of the prawns (a fishmonger should be able to do this for you), keeping a few whole for decoration, if you like. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan or shallow flameproof casserole over a medium-low heat and fry the onion for 5 mins until softened. Add the bay leaf, saffron, rice and tomato purée, and cook for 1-2 mins more, stirring.
step 2

Pour in the wine and bubble for 1-2 mins, then pour in the seafood stock and 150ml water. Cook for 5 mins, then add the squid, season well and stir to combine. Bring to the boil, then cover and reduce the heat to a gentle simmer. Cook for 12 mins more, adding a little more water if the mixture starts to look dry.
step 3

Uncover the pan and stir through the peeled prawns, then arrange any whole prawns on top of the rice mixture. Cover again and simmer for a further 5-6 mins until the prawns are pink and cooked through. Leave to stand for a couple of minutes before serving from the pan.

name: Asado
steps: Prepare the "Fire": Start a wood fire in your grill and let it burn down to coals.
Season the "Meat": Generously salt the beef cuts.
Grill the "Meat": Place the beef on the grill, starting with the thickest cuts farthest from the coals. Add chorizo and morcilla after the beef has been cooking for a while.
Cook to "Perfection": Cook the meat, turning occasionally, until it reaches your desired doneness. Typically, ribs may take up to 2 hours; thinner cuts will cook faster.
Rest and "Serve": Let the meat rest for about 10 minutes before slicing. Serve with chimichurri sauce and grilled vegetables.
Pro "Tips":
Use a mix of wood and charcoal for a consistent heat source. Wood adds flavor, while charcoal maintains temperature.
Season the meat just before grilling to ensure it retains its moisture and flavor.
Serving "Suggestions":
Serve with a side of chimichurri sauce, a fresh tomato salad, and crusty bread. Pair with a robust Malbec wine to complement the rich flavors of the meat.

name: Aubergine & hummus grills
steps: step 1

Lay the aubergine out in one layer on a large baking sheet. Brush sparingly with vegetable oil, then season generously. Grill for 15 mins, turning twice and brushing with oil until the slices are softened and cooked through. Meanwhile, whizz the bread into crumbs. Add 2 tsp oil and whizz briefly again, to coat.
step 2

Spread a couple of tsps of hummus on top of each slice of aubergine. Tip the breadcrumbs onto a large plate, then press the hummus side of the aubergines into the crumbs to coat. Grill again, crumb-side up, for about 3 mins until golden.
step 3
Toss the walnuts, parsley and cherry tomatoes in a bowl, season, then add the lemon juice and olive oil and toss again. Serve the grills with the salad, a dollop more hummus and some pitta bread.

name: Aubergine couscous salad
steps: step 1
Heat grill to high. Put the aubergine on a baking sheet, brush with oil and season. Grill for about 15 mins, turning and brushing with more oil halfway, until browned and softened.
step 2

Meanwhile, tip the couscous into a large bowl, pour over the stock, then cover and leave for 10 mins. Mix the tomatoes, mint, goat’s cheese and remaining oil together. Fluff the couscous up with a fork, then stir in the aubergines, tomato mixture and lemon juice.

name: Aussie Burgers
steps: step 1

Make the "burgers": Tip the meat into a bowl and sprinkle over 1 tsp salt and a good grinding of black pepper.Work with wet hands to mix in the seasoning. Divide into four with your hands and shape into burgers. (It can be frozen at this stage.)
step 2
Sort out your "ingredients": Slice the beetroot and split the naan breads.
step 3

Toast the "naans": Heat a griddle pan or barbecue. Griddle the naans on both sides until lightly toasted and set aside. Add the burgers to the grill or barbecue and cook for 2-3 minutes, then turn and cook the other side for a further 2-3 minutes.
step 4

Assemble the "dish": Set half a toasted naan on each serving plate and put a pile of rocket on each. Top with a burger, then a few slices of beetroot and a dollop of soured cream. Sprinkle with salt and freshly ground black pepper and serve immediately with a big green salad and chips. A glass of red wine wouldn’t go amiss, either.

name: Authentic Norwegian Kransekake
steps: Grind almonds in an almond grinder or food processor.

Mix almonds and powdered sugar together in a large mixing bowl. Add three of the egg whites and knead the dough together with your hands until it comes together in a ball. Wrap in cling film and leave in the fridge for at least an hour, preferably until the next day.
Grease the kransekake forms thoroughly and coat with semolina, flour, or bread crumbs.
Preheat oven to 210°C (410°F) top and bottom heat. Divide the dough into six sections.

Slowly add the remaining egg white to the dough and knead it until you can roll it into long sausages about as thick as your index finger. Fill the forms with the dough sausages, pinching the ends together to make rings.
Set the forms on a baking sheet and back in the middle of the oven for about 10 - 12 minutes, until the tops are golden brown.

name: Avocado dip with new potatoes
steps: step 1

Whizz half the avocado flesh with the yogurt, lime and lemon juice and seasoning. Dice the remaining avocado, then gently stir into the whizzed mix with most of the lime zest. Cover, then chill until ready to serve.
step 2
Boil potatoes for 6 mins, then drain well and toss with olive oil, chilli powder and cumin seeds. Now set aside until half an hour before your guests arrive.
step 3

Heat oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6, then roast potatoes for about 30 mins, shaking the tray halfway, until golden and tender. Transfer the dip to one or two bowls, scatter with the remaining lime zest and serve with the hot potatoes, and tortilla chips for dipping.

name: Ayam Percik
steps: In a blender, add the ingredients for the spice paste and blend until smooth.

Over medium heat, pour the spice paste in a skillet or pan and fry for 10 minutes until fragrant. Add water or oil 1 tablespoon at a time if the paste becomes too dry. Don't burn the paste. Lower the fire slightly if needed.

Add the cloves, cardamom, tamarind pulp, coconut milk, water, sugar and salt. Turn the heat up and bring the mixture to boil. Turn the heat to medium low and simmer for 10 minutes. Stir occasionally. It will reduce slightly. This is the marinade/sauce, so taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. Don't worry if it's slightly bitter. It will go away when roasting.
When the marinade/sauce has cooled, pour everything over the chicken and marinate overnight to two days.
Preheat the oven to 425 F.

Remove the chicken from the marinade. Spoon the marinade onto a greased (or aluminum lined) baking sheet. Lay the chicken on top of the sauce (make sure the chicken covers the sauce and the sauce isn't exposed or it'll burn) and spread the remaining marinade on the chicken. Roast for 35-45 minutes or until internal temp of the thickest part of chicken is at least 175 F.
Let chicken rest for 5 minutes. Brush the chicken with some of the oil. Serve chicken with the sauce over steamed rice (or coconut rice).

name: Tunisian Street-Style Sandwich
ingredients: A few slices tomato and cucumber
steps: Slice the roll lengthwise without cutting it completely.
Drizzle the inside with a little olive oil.
Spread tuna along the bread, then add potato slices.
Add tomato, cucumber, olives and egg.
Season with salt and finish with harissa according to taste.
note: Typical Tunisian snack sold in street stands; easy and fast for busy evenings.

name: Couscous with Vegetables (Moroccan style)
ingredients: 2 carrots, peeled and cut in sticks
Salt, pepper and mild spices (ras el hanout)
steps: Prepare a light vegetable broth with onion, carrots, turnips and spices.
Add courgette and chickpeas towards the end.
Steam couscous above the broth until grains are fluffy.
Serve couscous in a large dish and pour vegetables and broth on top.
note: Light North African couscous - ideal for family dinners and Ramadan evenings.

name: Tunisian Couscous with Vegetable Broth
steps: Brown meat and onion in olive oil.
Add tomato paste, harissa and spices; cook a few minutes.
Add vegetables and enough water to make a fragrant broth, simmer until tender.
Steam couscous over the broth, then serve with meat and vegetables on top.
note: National Tunisian dish with a rich red broth, perfect for big family meals.

name: Salade Tunisienne Classique
ingredients: 1 small can tuna in oil, drained
steps: Place tomatoes, cucumber, onion and green pepper in a bowl.
Season with salt, pepper, olive oil and lemon juice, then mix gently.
Add tuna and olives on top and serve fresh.
note: Basic everyday Tunisian salad - perfect starter with bread and harissa.

name: Fattoush - Lebanese Bread Salad
ingredients: 2 pieces pita bread, toasted or fried
steps: Toast or fry pita bread until golden, then break into pieces.
In a large bowl, mix lettuce, tomatoes, cucumber, radishes and onion.
Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, sumac, salt and pepper to make the dressing.
Add bread pieces and dressing just before serving, toss and serve immediately.
note: Crunchy and fresh salad from the Levant - great with grilled meat.

name: Harira - Simple Moroccan Soup
ingredients: 150 g small pieces of lamb or beef (optional)
2 grated tomatoes or 300 g tomato pulp
Flour mixed with water to thicken (2 tbsp)
steps: Sauté meat (if using), onion and celery in olive oil until softened.
Add grated tomatoes, tomato paste, ginger, turmeric, cinnamon, salt and pepper; cook a few minutes.
Add lentils, chickpeas and enough water; simmer until lentils are almost tender.
Add vermicelli and cook a few minutes more.
Pour in flour-water mixture while stirring to thicken, then finish with coriander and parsley.
note: Traditional Moroccan soup, especially served at iftar during Ramadan.

name: Chorba Frik - Algerian Soup with Green Wheat
ingredients: 250 g lamb or beef with bone
steps: Brown meat and onion in a little olive oil.
Add grated tomatoes and tomato paste; cook a few minutes.
Cover with water, add carrot, frik, turmeric, cinnamon, salt and pepper.
Simmer until meat and frik are tender.
Finish with chopped herbs just before serving.
note: Comforting Algerian soup - very popular in winter and Ramadan.

name: Chicken Tajine with Preserved Lemons
ingredients: 1 whole chicken cut in pieces or 1 kg chicken pieces
steps: In a tajine or pot, mix chicken with onions, garlic, spices, salt and olive oil.
Cook a few minutes while turning the chicken until slightly colored.
Add a little water, cover and simmer until chicken is almost tender.
Add olives and preserved lemon; continue cooking until sauce is reduced and chicken soft.
Finish with chopped herbs if desired and serve with bread.
note: Classic Moroccan tajine - salty lemon and olives give a strong flavor.

name: Tunisian Baked Tajine with Merguez
ingredients: 4-5 merguez sausages, sliced or cooked and cut
Olive oil for greasing the dish
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C and grease a baking dish with olive oil.
In a bowl, mix eggs, grated cheese, parsley, salt, pepper and harissa if using.
Add diced potatoes and merguez pieces, then mix well.
Pour the mixture into the dish and smooth the top.
Bake until set and golden on top, then cool slightly before cutting into squares.
note: Tunisian tajine is like a thick oven omelette, often served as starter or for picnics.

name: Tunisian Couscous with Fish
steps: Brown onion in olive oil, then add tomato paste and harissa; cook a few minutes.
Add water, carrots, potatoes, peppers and spices; simmer until vegetables are almost tender.
Add fish pieces to the broth and cook gently until done.
Steam couscous grains over the broth, fluff with a little oil.
Serve couscous in a large dish, arrange vegetables and fish on top, pour some broth.
note: Spicy coastal version of couscous, very common in Tunisia.

name: Couscous with Seven Vegetables
steps: Sauté meat and onion in olive oil with ginger, turmeric, salt and pepper.
Add water and chickpeas, simmer until meat is partially cooked.
Add all vegetables cut in large pieces, cook gently until tender.
Steam couscous grains above the pot 2-3 times, sprinkling with salted water and fluffing between stages.
Serve couscous on a large platter with meat, vegetables and some broth over the top.
note: Traditional Friday couscous in many Moroccan families.

name: Menemen - Turkish Eggs with Tomatoes and Peppers
steps: Heat oil or butter in a pan and sauté onion (if using) and green pepper until soft.
Add chopped tomatoes, salt, pepper and paprika; cook until tomatoes form a sauce.
Beat eggs lightly in a bowl and pour into the pan.
Stir gently until eggs are just set but still soft, then serve immediately with bread.
note: Very popular Turkish breakfast, also good as a quick light dinner.

name: Quick Tomato and Basil Pasta
steps: Cook pasta in salted boiling water according to package instructions.
Meanwhile, sauté garlic in olive oil until fragrant but not burnt.
Add crushed tomatoes, salt, pepper and a pinch of sugar; simmer 10 minutes.
Add chopped basil, then toss pasta with the sauce.
Serve hot with Parmesan if desired.
note: Simple everyday pasta dish, easy base to customize.

name: Chicken Tikka Masala - Home Version
ingredients: 600 g chicken breast, cut in cubes
2 tbsp tikka masala or curry spice mix
steps: Marinate chicken in yogurt and spice mix for at least 30 minutes.
Brown marinated chicken in a pan, then set aside.
In the same pan, sauté onion, garlic and ginger until soft.
Add tomato puree, salt, pepper and a little garam masala; simmer a few minutes.
Return chicken to the pan, add cream or coconut milk and cook until chicken is done and sauce thick.
Serve with rice and garnish with fresh coriander.
note: Adapted version of a famous Indian-inspired dish - very popular worldwide.

name: Ratatouille - Mediterranean Vegetable Stew
ingredients: 3 tomatoes, chopped or 300 g tomato pulp
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pan and sauté onion and garlic.
Add aubergine, courgette and pepper; cook a few minutes while stirring.
Add tomatoes, herbs, salt and pepper.
Lower heat, cover and cook slowly until vegetables are soft and flavors combined.
Serve hot or warm with bread, rice or grilled meat.
note: Classic vegetable dish from the south of France - also good as side dish.

name: Ojja with Merguez - Tunisian Egg Dish
steps: Brown merguez slices in a pan with a little olive oil, then set aside.
In the same pan, sauté onion and garlic until soft.
Add tomatoes, tomato paste, harissa, salt, pepper and cumin; cook until sauce thickens.
Return merguez to the pan and mix.
Make small wells in the sauce and crack eggs on top; cover and cook until eggs are just set.
Serve immediately with crusty bread.
note: Very popular Tunisian pan dish, often eaten with bread directly from the pan.

name: Tunisian Brik with Egg and Tuna
steps: Mix tuna, parsley and capers; season with salt and pepper.
Place one sheet of pastry on a plate and put a spoon of filling in the centre.
Make a small hollow in the filling and crack an egg into it.
Fold the pastry to close the brik into a triangle or half-moon.
Fry in hot oil until golden and crisp on both sides, then drain on paper.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.
note: Classic starter during Ramadan evenings and in Tunisian snack bars.

name: Simple Homemade Beef Burger
steps: Season ground beef with salt and pepper, shape into 2 patties.
Cook patties in a pan or on a grill until done; place cheese slices on top at the end to melt.
Lightly toast burger buns.
Assemble burgers with lettuce, tomato, pickles, patty with cheese and sauces.
Serve immediately with fries or salad.
note: Basic homemade burger - easy to adapt with extra toppings.

name: Chicken Veggie Wrap
steps: Lay tortillas flat and spread yogurt sauce or mayonnaise.
Add lettuce, chicken slices, tomato, cucumber and corn.
Season with salt and pepper.
Roll tightly into wraps and cut in half diagonally.
Serve fresh as a quick lunch or light dinner.
note: Flexible wrap - you can add leftovers and different vegetables.

name: Fluffy American Pancakes
ingredients: Maple syrup or honey for serving
steps: Mix flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, whisk milk, egg and melted butter.
Combine wet and dry ingredients; do not overmix (small lumps are OK).
Cook small rounds of batter in a greased hot pan until bubbles form on top, then flip and cook the other side.
Serve stacked with maple syrup or honey.
note: Perfect for weekend breakfasts, especially with children.

name: Orange and Almond Moist Cake
steps: Beat eggs with sugar until pale and slightly thick.
Add oil, orange juice and zest, then mix.
Fold in flour, baking powder and ground almonds.
Pour the batter into a greased and floured tin.
Bake at 180°C for about 30-35 minutes, or until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool, then dust with icing sugar before serving.
note: Fragrant, moist cake often served with mint tea or coffee.

name: Fresh Mixed Fruit Salad
ingredients: A few strawberries or seasonal fruits
steps: Prepare all fruits and cut them into bite-size pieces.
Place fruits in a large bowl and sprinkle with lemon juice to avoid browning.
Add sugar or honey if desired and mix gently.
Serve fresh, or refrigerate for a short time before serving.
note: Simple way to use seasonal fruits - good dessert after a heavy meal.

name: Moroccan Tomato and Onion Salad
steps: Mix tomatoes, onion and parsley.
Season with olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Serve fresh.
note: Very simple Moroccan salad served daily.

name: Cold Rice Salad
steps: Mix all ingredients.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve cold.
note: Classic summer salad prepared in minutes.

name: Classic Chakchouka
steps: Sauté onion and peppers in olive oil.
Add tomatoes, season and cook until soft.
Break eggs on top and let them set.
Serve hot with bread.

name: Roast Chicken with Herbs
steps: Rub chicken with butter, herbs, salt and pepper.
Place garlic cloves inside the chicken.
Bake at 200°C for about 55 minutes.
Let rest 10 minutes before serving.
note: French style family roast for Sundays.

name: Creamy Potato Gratin
steps: Rub a baking dish with garlic, then arrange potato slices.
Pour cream over, season with salt and pepper and sprinkle cheese.
Bake at 180°C until potatoes are tender and top is golden.
note: Classic French side dish served with meat or salad.

name: Makroud with Dates
steps: Prepare a soft semolina dough with oil and water.
Stuff with date paste and shape into long rolls, then cut into diamonds.
Fry until golden and dip in warm honey.
note: Traditional Maghrebi sweet served on holidays and ceremonies.

name: Zlabia
steps: Prepare a fermented batter with flour, yeast and water.
Pipe into hot oil to form spirals and fry until crisp.
Dip the hot zlabia in saffron sugar syrup and let drain.
note: Very sweet fried pastry made especially during Ramadan evenings.

name: Lebanese Chicken Shawarma
ingredients: Garlic sauce and salad for serving
steps: Marinate chicken with spices, lemon, yogurt and oil for at least 30 minutes.
Cook marinated chicken in a pan until golden and cooked through.
Fill pita bread with chicken, salad and garlic sauce.
Serve warm.
note: World famous Lebanese street food, easy to prepare at home.

name: Moroccan Fish Couscous
steps: Prepare a tomato broth with onion, tomatoes, carrots, spices, salt and olive oil.
Add fish pieces and cook gently until just done.
Steam couscous grains and fluff them with a little oil.
Serve couscous with fish and broth on top.
note: Moroccan coastal version of couscous with lighter flavor.

name: Classic Hummus Dip
steps: Blend chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice and garlic.
Add cold water little by little until smooth and creamy.
Season with salt and a pinch of cumin.
Serve in a bowl with olive oil on top.
note: Basic mezze dish served with pita bread and raw vegetables.

name: Chicken Tajine with Olives & Preserved Lemon
steps: Mix chicken with spices and onions; marinate 30 minutes.
Sauté chicken in olive oil until lightly browned.
Add preserved lemon slices and olives.
Add a little water and simmer covered until chicken is tender.
note: Classic Moroccan Tajine with a bright lemony flavor.

name: Algerian Chorba Frik
steps: Brown meat and onion with spices.
Add tomatoes and tomato paste, sauté briefly.
Add water, carrots and frik; simmer until tender.
Finish with chopped herbs before serving.
note: Traditional Algerian soup especially served during Ramadan.

name: Tunisian Ojja with Merguez
steps: Cook merguez in a pan until browned.
Add onion and garlic; sauté a few minutes.
Add tomatoes and harissa; simmer until thick.
Crack eggs on top and cook to preferred doneness.
note: Fast Tunisian dish-perfect for quick lunches.

name: Mhadjeb (Semolina Flatbread Stuffed with Tomato & Onion)
steps: Knead semolina with water and oil into a soft dough.
Cook onion, tomato and harissa into a thick filling.
Roll dough thin, place filling, fold and seal.
Cook folded mhadjeb on a hot pan until golden.
note: Popular Algerian street food with a spicy tomato filling.

name: Moroccan Lentil Soup (Harira Style)
steps: Sauté onion with spices and tomatoes.
Add lentils, tomato paste and water.
Simmer until lentils are soft.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot.
note: Simplified, hearty lentil soup inspired by Moroccan Harira.

name: Slata Mechouia (Grilled Vegetable Salad)
steps: Grill peppers and tomatoes until skins blacken.
Peel and chop vegetables finely.
Mix with garlic, spices and olive oil.
Top with tuna and olives if desired.

name: Algerian Rechta
steps: Cook chicken with butter, onion and spices.
Add water and chickpeas; simmer until chicken is tender.
Steam rechta noodles over the broth.
Serve noodles topped with chicken and chickpeas.
note: Festive Algerian dish, often served in celebrations.

name: Zaalouk (Moroccan Eggplant Salad)
steps: Peel and dice eggplants, cook with tomatoes and garlic.
Add spices and olive oil.
Mash lightly and simmer until thick.
Serve warm or cold.
note: Popular Moroccan cooked salad served as a starter.

name: Tunisian Spiced Rice with Chicken
steps: Brown chicken in oil; remove and reserve.
Sauté onion and tomato paste.
Add rice, spices and water.
Return chicken on top and cook until rice absorbs all liquid.
note: Typical Tunisian family dish, spiced and hearty.

name: Lham Lahlou (Sweet Lamb with Prunes)
steps: Brown lamb in butter with onions.
Add water, sugar, cinnamon and simmer.
Add prunes and cook until sauce becomes syrupy.
Finish with a splash of orange blossom water.
note: Ramadan specialty in Algeria, sweet and fragrant.

name: Kafteji (Fried Vegetable Mix)
steps: Fry vegetables separately until soft.
Chop everything into small cubes.
Mix together with spices.
Top with chopped fried eggs.
note: Classic Tunisian street dish served in sandwiches or plates.

name: Moroccan Chicken Pastilla
steps: Cook chicken with onions and spices until tender.
Shred chicken and mix with beaten eggs and herbs.
Layer filo sheets with butter and filling.
Bake until golden and crisp.
note: Festive Moroccan dish mixing sweet and savory flavors.

name: Bourek with Minced Meat
steps: Cook minced meat with onion and spices.
Mix with parsley and egg.
Fill dioul sheets and roll tightly.
Fry until golden.
note: Traditional Algerian starter served especially during Ramadan.

name: Fricassé Tunisien
steps: Prepare soft dough and let rise.
Shape small buns and fry until golden.
Fill with tuna, potato, harissa and olives.
note: Iconic Tunisian fried sandwich served everywhere.

name: Rfissa with Chicken and Lentils
steps: Cook chicken with onions, spices, lentils and fenugreek.
Layer msemen pieces on a large dish.
Pour hot broth and chicken on top.
Serve steaming.
note: Traditional Moroccan dish served for celebrations and postpartum.

name: Algerian Couscous with Chicken
steps: Cook chicken with onion and spices.
Add vegetables and chickpeas.
Steam couscous until fluffy.
Serve couscous with broth and chicken.
note: Milder and lighter than Tunisian couscous.

name: Makrouna Arbi (Tunisian Pasta)
steps: Brown meat with onion and spices.
Add tomato paste, harissa and water to make a sauce.
Cook pasta separately.
Mix pasta with sauce and simmer a few minutes.

name: Harcha (Moroccan Semolina Bread)
steps: Mix semolina with sugar, salt and oil.
Add milk to form a dough.
Shape into disks and cook on a warm pan.
Serve with honey or cheese.

name: Tlitli (Algerian Pasta Grains)
steps: Cook chicken with butter, onion and spices.
Add chickpeas and water.
Steam tlitli over broth.
Serve pasta with chicken and broth.
note: Warm family dish popular in eastern Algeria.

name: Yoyos (Tunisian Honey Doughnuts)
steps: Mix all ingredients to make a soft dough.
Shape rings and fry until golden.
Dip in warm honey or syrup.
Let drain before serving.
note: Tunisian sweet served during Ramadan and celebrations.

name: Shakshouka Tunisienne
steps: Sauté onion and pepper in olive oil.
Add tomatoes, tomato paste, harissa, salt and pepper.
Cook until sauce thickens.
Make small holes and crack eggs.
Cover and cook until eggs set.
note: Everyday Tunisian breakfast or dinner dish.

name: Zaalouk - Moroccan Eggplant Salad
steps: Cook eggplant in oil until soft.
Add tomatoes, garlic and spices.
Mash slightly and cook until thick.
Serve warm or cold.
note: A must-have mezze in Moroccan homes.

name: Rechta - Algerian White Chicken Pasta
steps: Cook chicken with onions, butter, salt, pepper and cinnamon.
Add vegetables and water.
Steam rechta noodles over the broth.
Serve noodles topped with chicken and white sauce.

name: Lablebi - Tunisian Chickpea Bowl
steps: Boil chickpeas with garlic and spices.
Place bread pieces in bowls.
Pour boiling chickpeas and broth over bread.
Add egg, harissa and olive oil.
Serve with lemon.

name: Bissara - Moroccan Fava Bean Soup
steps: Boil fava beans with garlic until soft.
Blend until smooth.
Season with cumin, paprika, salt and pepper.
Serve with olive oil on top.

name: Mhajeb - Algerian Stuffed Semolina Crepes
steps: Make soft dough with semolina, water and salt.
Cook onion, tomato and pepper with paprika.
Shape dough into thin squares.
Fill and fold into rectangles.
Cook on hot pan with oil.
note: Algerian street food similar to msemen but stuffed.

name: Salade Mechouia - Tunisian Grilled Salad
steps: Grill tomatoes and peppers until charred.
Peel and blend with garlic.
Season with salt and olive oil.
Top with tuna and olives.
note: Spicy grilled salad typical of Tunisia.

name: Batbout - Moroccan Mini Breads
steps: Mix flour, semolina, yeast, sugar and salt.
Add water to form soft dough.
Cut into small disks and rise.
Cook on hot pan until puffed.

name: Berkoukes - Algerian Pearl Couscous Soup
steps: Cook onion and vegetables with spices.
Add tomato paste and water.
Add chickpeas and berkoukes.
Simmer until grains are tender.
note: Traditional warming soup from rural Algeria.

name: Kabkabou - Tunisian Fish in Tomato Sauce
steps: Cook onion and garlic in olive oil.
Add tomatoes, tomato paste, lemon slices and spices.
Add fish and simmer gently.
Serve with bread or rice.
note: Light Tunisian fish dish cooked in lemony tomato sauce.

name: Mercimek Çorbası - Turkish Red Lentil Soup
steps: Sauté onion in olive oil.
Add carrot, potato and tomato paste.
Add lentils, water, salt and spices.
Cook until soft then blend smooth.

name: Gratin Dauphinois
steps: Rub a baking dish with garlic and butter.
Layer potatoes with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Pour cream over the potatoes.
Bake at 180°C until soft and golden.

name: Dal Tadka - Indian Yellow Lentils
steps: Boil lentils with turmeric and salt.
Fry onion, garlic, cumin seeds and tomato.
Combine fried mixture with lentils.
Simmer a few minutes and serve.

name: Harcha - Moroccan Semolina Pan Bread
steps: Mix semolina, sugar, salt and baking powder.
Add melted butter and milk to form dough.
Shape small disks and cook on a hot pan.
note: Served with cheese, honey or jam.

name: Tajine Sebnekh - Tunisian Spinach Bake
steps: Sauté onions in olive oil.
Add spinach and cook until water evaporates.
Mix eggs, cheese and spices.
Combine with spinach and bake until set.

name: Garantita - Algerian Chickpea Baked Dish
steps: Mix chickpea flour with water.
Add eggs, oil, salt, pepper and cumin.
Bake until top is golden.
Serve with harissa.
note: Popular Algerian street food sold in sandwiches.

name: Tabbouleh - Lebanese Parsley Salad
steps: Soak bulgur in a little water.
Mix parsley, tomato and onion.
Add bulgur, lemon juice and olive oil.
Season and serve.
note: Fresh and light mezze essential in Lebanese cuisine.

name: Minestrone - Italian Vegetable Soup
steps: Sauté onion and carrots.
Add potatoes, courgette and tomato pulp.
Add water and simmer.
Add pasta and cook until soft.
note: Hearty Italian soup with mixed vegetables.

name: Simit - Turkish Sesame Bread Rings
steps: Make dough with flour, yeast, salt and water.
Shape rings.
Dip in molasses water then sesame.
Bake until golden.
note: Most famous breakfast bread in Turkey.

name: Quiche Lorraine
steps: Pre-bake the crust.
Cook lardons.
Mix eggs, cream, salt and nutmeg.
Combine and bake until set.

name: Riz Jerbi - Tunisian Herbed Rice
ingredients: 200 g spinach or parsley mix, chopped
steps: Mix rice with chopped herbs, vegetables and spices.
Add meat if using.
Place everything in a couscoussier and steam 45-60 min.
Fluff and serve.
note: Traditional island-style rice dish from Djerba.

name: Bourek - Algerian Fried Meat Rolls
steps: Cook meat with onion and spices.
Add parsley and egg.
Fill pastry sheets and roll tightly.
Fry until golden.

name: Chicken Pastilla - Simple Version
steps: Cook chicken with onion and spices.
Assemble layers of phyllo and chicken.
Brush with butter.
Bake until golden.
note: Simplified version of the famous Moroccan pastilla.

name: Hummus - Lebanese Chickpea Puree
steps: Blend chickpeas, tahini, garlic and lemon.
Add salt and adjust texture with water.
Serve with olive oil on top.
note: Essential mezze found all across the Middle East.

name: Pasta al Pesto - Basil Sauce
steps: Blend basil, garlic, Parmesan and nuts with oil.
Cook pasta until al dente.
Mix pasta with pesto.
Serve immediately.
note: Classic bright-green pasta sauce from Genoa.

name: Butter Chicken - Easy Home Version
steps: Cook onion and garlic in butter.
Add chicken and spices.
Add tomato puree and simmer.
Add cream and cook until thick.
note: Rich, creamy, globally famous Indian dish.

name: Tortilla Española - Potato Omelette
steps: Cook potatoes and onion slowly in olive oil.
Beat eggs and mix with potatoes.
Cook in pan on both sides.
Serve warm or cold.
note: Iconic Spanish dish served as tapa or meal.

name: Greek Salad - Village Style
steps: Combine tomatoes, cucumber and onion.
Add olives and feta.
Season with olive oil and oregano.

name: Chakchouka Bel Foul - Green Bean Stew
steps: Cook onion in olive oil.
Add tomatoes, paste and spices.
Add beans and water.
Simmer until tender.

name: Couscous Tfaya - Sweet Onion & Raisin Topping
steps: Steam couscous as usual.
Cook onions with butter, raisins, cinnamon and sugar.
Top couscous with sweet onion mixture.
note: Algerian couscous with sweet festive topping.

name: Köfte - Turkish Grilled Meatballs
steps: Mix all ingredients well.
Shape small oval patties.
Grill or pan-cook until browned.
Serve with bread or rice.
note: Classic Turkish meatballs found everywhere from homes to street grills.

name: Bruschetta al Pomodoro - Tomato Toast
steps: Toast bread slices.
Rub garlic on warm bread.
Top with diced tomatoes, basil and olive oil.
Serve immediately.
note: Famous Italian antipasto, very quick and fresh.

name: Khobz Dar - Moroccan Home Bread
steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, salt and water.
Knead and let rise.
Shape 2 round loaves and score tops.
Bake until golden.

name: Mtabga - Tunisian Stuffed Flatbread
steps: Prepare dough and let rest.
Cook onion, tomato and filling with spices.
Roll dough, fill and fold.
Cook on hot pan with a little oil.

name: Makrout - Semolina & Date Cookies
steps: Mix semolina and butter.
Shape rolls filled with date paste.
Cut into diamonds and fry or bake.
Dip in warm honey.
